content:
It is dirty truth about Indian banking, but your solution is economic suicide.
​You are 100% right on the disease: private banks have turned into glorified pawnshops—funding 6% luxury cars and overpriced 2BHKs for urban elites while dumping actual productive risk (farmers and MSMEs) onto 30%+ extortionate NBFCs. The Loan Against Property (LAP) addiction is a ticking time bomb.
​But your cure is delusional. Handing ₹100 Lakh Crore back to state-owned banks? Have we already forgotten the ₹10 Lakh Crore PSU NPA catastrophe that taxpayers had to bail out? You don't break a private cartel by running back to a bureaucratic graveyard.
​Here is the question no banker on this feed wants to answer: Are you actually managing credit risk to build India’s economy, or are you just running an asset-backed pawnshop until the real estate bubble pops?
comment: The missing piece is credit underwriting quality. Whether public or private, weak risk assessment turns any lending model into a liability. The real reform is incentives, not ownership alone.
